title: Machine Intuition Research Brief — October 7, 2026

entries.title: SemEval-2026 Task 12: Abductive Event Reasoning
entries.development: The authors introduce an evidence-grounded benchmark that asks systems to select the most plausible direct cause of a target event from distributed supporting material and non-causal distractors. The shared task drew 122 participants and 518 submissions.
entries.significance: This is a close formal analogue to Pattern Sense followed by Inference Engine review: candidate relationships must be distinguished from background correlation and semantic resemblance.
entries.implications: Build an internal evaluation set with direct causes, enabling conditions, common causes and merely related facts labeled separately. Score retrieval and causal selection independently.
entries.uncertainty: The benchmark is multiple choice and rewards one selected cause. Real investigations may contain several interacting causes or no adequate candidate.

entries.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Causal Discovery: a Constraint-based, Argumentation-driven Approach
entries.development: Causal Assumption-based Argumentation combines conditional-independence evidence with structural priors elicited from an LLM. The authors report state-of-the-art benchmark performance and add a protocol intended to reduce memorization bias.
entries.significance: The method treats language-model knowledge as defeasible expert testimony rather than causal truth, while preserving a symbolic account of which constraints support each graph.
entries.implications: Let Pattern Sense propose directional priors with explicit source and confidence. The Inference Engine should accept, reject or leave edges unresolved according to statistical constraints, retaining the argument trail.
entries.uncertainty: Results use standard benchmarks and semantically grounded synthetic graphs. Performance on sparse, contested OSINT evidence is unproven.

entries.title: Automated Hypothesis Validation with Agentic Sequential Falsifications
entries.sourceDate: Published May 1, 2025; modified June 18, 2025; newly identified.
entries.development: POPPER converts a free-form hypothesis into measurable implications, designs sequential falsification tests and applies Type-I error control across observations. The authors report six-domain evaluations, comparable biological-hypothesis validation to human scientists and roughly tenfold time reduction.
entries.significance: It supplies a rigorous answer to hypothesis proliferation: Machine Intuition can generate freely, but promotion should depend on surviving pre-specified attempts at disconfirmation.
entries.implications: For each Inference Engine hypothesis, create a falsification queue, define stopping rules before testing and prevent repeated searches from silently inflating confidence.
entries.uncertainty: Agents may choose weak or redundant tests, and the headline comparison to scientists is domain- and task-dependent. Statistical error control does not guarantee valid measurement.

entries.title: Extending Complex Logical Queries on Uncertain Knowledge Graphs
entries.sourceDate: Published January 1, 2025; modified September 18, 2025; newly identified.
entries.development: The paper introduces soft logical queries over incomplete, uncertain knowledge graphs and combines forward inference with backward calibration. The authors provide a theoretical argument against catastrophic cascading error while retaining the complexity of existing first-order query methods, plus benchmark experiments.
entries.significance: Pattern Sense often composes several individually weak links. This work directly addresses how uncertainty should travel through multi-hop relational queries instead of being replaced by a single opaque score.
entries.implications: Represent relations as graded assertions, propagate uncertainty during candidate discovery, then calibrate backward from the query before Second Sight displays a conclusion.
entries.uncertainty: The formal guarantees depend on the model assumptions and tested query language. They do not address deceptive sources, correlated reports or temporal change by themselves.

entries.title: The Bayesian audit: evaluating the proportionality of scientific claims to evidence
entries.development: The authors propose a six-step claim-centered audit: isolate the claim, state priors, translate evidence into a likelihood measure, update to a posterior, test sensitivity across plausible priors and write a conclusion proportional to the result. A social-priming case illustrates the procedure.
entries.significance: The framework connects evidentiary calculation to language discipline. It prevents a modest probability update from becoming an absolute public claim.
entries.implications: Add an audit object to the Inference Engine containing claim text, alternatives, prior range, Bayes factor or likelihood proxy, posterior range, sensitivity result and an allowed-language tier.
entries.uncertainty: The paper is methodological and illustrative, not a new empirical validation study. Priors and likelihood approximations remain contestable, and poor source data cannot be repaired by Bayesian arithmetic.

nextMoves: Build a small abductive benchmark from past IMDO cases with direct cause, enabling condition, common cause and non-causal association labels.
Prototype a hypothesis record that combines defeasible edge arguments, a pre-registered falsification queue and sequential error control.
Define public-language tiers tied to posterior ranges and sensitivity results rather than a single confidence number.
